contamination.detail: NOT a blind read, and this must be weighed when reading the edit count. 2-030 is the corpus's only page with ground truth and no proposal — it was adjudicated by the eScriptorium route before this pass existed — so there is no mz/ocr prediction to key against and the only line geometry available is gt/ocr's own, reached through `harness ocr lines 2-030`, which prints the stored text beside every index. I therefore saw the existing ground truth before reading the raster. Every line below was nevertheless re-read off the 300 dpi scan at 2x and, where a doubt was nameable, at 4x; the three changes proposed are changes AGAINST what I had already seen, not agreements with it. But an unchanged line here is weaker evidence than an unchanged line on a blind page, because anchoring cannot be ruled out. The compass diagram (fig. 213) prints all 27 terms a second time in italic and is a genuine independent witness on this page; I used it only where noted (line 26).

footnotes: None on this page. The counting invariants (spec 2.10) are vacuous here, not passed.

notes.page: Scan folio 304. Two-column gloss list under fig. 213, flanked by body prose above (lines 1-2) and below (lines 30-31). Every list entry is a Chukchee term plus an English gloss in curly quotes. `harness ocr gaps` reports no uncovered ink, so no line was dropped. Line indices are ALTO identities and are not consecutive in reading order (CLAUDE.md); lines 4-16 are the left column, 17-28 the right, interleaved by vpos.
notes.method: Read every line off the sheets first (`--margins`, which on this page widens each crop to the full PrintSpace and so shows both columns at once — the index's own line is the one at its hpos). Then 2x over the twelve lines carrying a nameable doubt, then 4x over seven. The dot-below calls were settled by CONTRAST, per keying_spec.md 5.1: lines 12 and 24 land in the same 4x sheet, and `em-g̣ɪnuˊn` there shows an unmistakable dot below its g while `am-gɪnoˊt` shows none. That pairing is the evidence for both readings, and it is worth stating because the two look like they should share a root ('mid-night' / 'mid-day') and I opened the page expecting one of them to be wrong.
notes.marks: `harness proposal marks 2-030` was run against this proposal and reports three things, all of which are answered above rather than dismissed. (1) `rare` names the three bare-g forms — `am-gɪnoˊt-aᵋloˊ` x2 and `am-gɪnoˊt-aᵋloˊwtɪ` — at 2.8% of the g axis. (2) `ratio` puts this page's g-dot share at 80.0% against a 96.8% prior and a per-page band whose floor is 100.0 over 6 pages, i.e. `outside: low` — no page in the prior carries a bare Tier-1 g at all. (3) `conflict` names `neˊlyiᵋ`/`neˊlyɪᵋ`, in_batch. I am not moving on any of them, and the reason is that the tool is measuring a real property of this page rather than a defect: 2-030 sets the `am-gɪnoˊt-` morpheme three times bare beside `em-g̣ɪnuˊn-` twice dotted, and the two appear together in one 4x sheet. But an 80% share under a 100% floor is precisely the shape of a page that should be re-read before it is accepted, so this belongs in front of the adjudicator rather than only in my reasoning. If the dots are there and I have missed them, all three lines move together and the reading of line 12 is the control that would have to be wrong too. Note the prior is leave-one-out, so 2-030's own stored bare g's are not in the 96.8%.

16.note: FLAG FOR THE ADJUDICATOR — the printed dot on this g sits ABOVE the bowl, not below it. At 4x it is a well-formed round dot at about x-height and I can find nothing below the descender; compare line 15 in the same 4x sheet, where the dot is unambiguously below. I have keyed g+U+0323 anyway, on two grounds that are both rules rather than readings: dot-above g is not in the inventory at all (it is spec 3's forbidden lookalike FOR g̣, so there is no sort to key), and `-rg̣ɪn` is spec 5.1's documented noun-forming suffix. But that means the keyed form does not reproduce what I see on the paper, which is exactly the kind of thing this pass is not allowed to settle by itself. A type defect, a shifted sort, or ink — a human should look. The stored ground truth already keys g̣ here, so nothing changes either way; the flag is new.
